questions.question: Tropheryma whipplei.

parts_raw.text: a) Give 3 clinical manifestations/syndromes.
b) What is pathognomonic on biopsy?
c) What is the initial treatment?

questions.model_answer: a) (1) Weight loss with chronic watery diarrhea/steatorrhea and malabsorption. (2) Chronic migratory, nondestructive, seronegative arthropathy of peripheral joints (often precedes diagnosis by years). (3) CNS disease (memory disorder, dementia, ophthalmoplegia, myoclonus) or culture-negative endocarditis. b) Small-intestinal (duodenal) lamina propria infiltrated by large foamy macrophages containing PAS-positive, diastase-resistant granular inclusions. c) Ceftriaxone 2 g IV daily for 2 weeks (induction), followed by oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 160/800 mg twice daily for at least 1 year.

cohort_answer.text: a) Malabsorption/diarrhea; Arthralgia; Neurologic (ataxia, focal deficits); Endocarditis; Lymphadenopathy. b) PAS positive macrophages, especially on small bowel biopsy. c) Generally Ceftriaxone + Septra upfront.

questions.question: Whipple's disease.

parts.text: What are THREE common clinical findings (on presentation) of Tropheryma whipplei infection?
What finding on tissue biopsy is pathognomonic of this infection?
Which specific antimicrobial is used initially to treat Tropheryma whipplei infection?

parts_raw.text: What are THREE common clinical findings (on presentation) of Tropheryma whipplei infection?
What finding on tissue biopsy is pathognomonic of this infection?
Which specific antimicrobial is used initially to treat Tropheryma whipplei infection?

questions.model_answer: a) (1) Weight loss (75-100%). (2) Arthropathy/migratory arthralgias (70-100%). (3) Diarrhea (70-85%), often with abdominal pain. b) PAS-positive, diastase-resistant foamy macrophages in the lamina propria of the small intestine. c) Ceftriaxone 2 g IV daily (initial parenteral induction, 2 weeks), then oral TMP-SMX for at least 1 year.

cohort_answer.text: Clinical findings: arthropathy, fevers, weight loss and diarrhea, neurologic symptoms (cognitive impairment, ataxia, ophthalmoplegia, supranuclear gaze palsy); oculomasticatory myorhythmia is pathognomonic. Biopsy: distended macrophages in the lamina propria containing PAS+ (diastase-resistant) granules (foamy macrophages). Treatment: Ceftriaxone followed by SXT (35 reports of acquired resistance/relapse with TMP-SMX alone; CRO has high MIC in vitro for intracellular organisms) OR Doxycycline + hydroxychloroquine (primary regimen on Sandford).

questions.question: You see a 45-year-old woman presenting with several months of fever, abdominal discomfort, diarrhea, and occasional headache. Blood cultures, stool cultures, stool ova and parasites, and HIV test have all been negative. She undergoes upper endoscopy, which demonstrates villous atrophy of the small bowel with macrophages with periodic acid-Schiff positive inclusions.

questions.model_answer: a) Classic Whipple disease. b) Tropheryma whipplei. c) A specific confirmatory test on the biopsy tissue: PCR (ideally two targets from different genes) and/or immunohistochemistry for T. whipplei. d) (1) CSF PCR for T. whipplei to exclude CNS involvement. (2) Echocardiography to assess for valvular/endocarditis involvement. e) Induction with ceftriaxone 2 g IV daily for 2 weeks, followed by oral TMP-SMX 160/800 mg twice daily for at least 1 year.

questions.question: Tropheryma whipplei.

parts_raw.text: A) 3 clinical manifestations/syndromes

questions.model_answer: (1) Weight loss. (2) Migratory, nondestructive, seronegative arthropathy. (3) Chronic diarrhea/malabsorption (alternatively a systemic syndrome: culture-negative endocarditis or CNS disease with dementia/ophthalmoplegia).

cohort_answer.text: Clinical manifestations: Arthralgia, Weight loss, Diarrhea, Abdominal pain. Syndromes: Culture negative endocarditis, CNS disease (dementia, encephalopathy), Uveitis, chorioretinitis

questions.question: Tropheryma whipplei.

parts_raw.text: B) Diagnostic finding on bx

questions.model_answer: PAS-positive, diastase-resistant foamy macrophages in the lamina propria of the small intestine (duodenum/jejunum).

cohort_answer.text: GI: foamy periodic acid Schiff (PAS) stain + macrophages in small intestine

questions.question: Tropheryma whipplei.

parts_raw.text: C) Initial tx

questions.model_answer: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV daily for 2 weeks (induction), followed by oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 160/800 mg twice daily for at least 1 year.
questions.cohort_conflict: Cohort lists penicillin as an initial option; Mandell specifies ceftriaxone as the standard induction, with penicillin/meropenem reserved as alternatives (endocarditis or allergy/relapse).

cohort_answer.text: Ceftriaxone or Penicillin x 2 weeks followed by TMP/SMX x 1 year

questions.question: Tropheryma whipplei.

parts_raw.text: D) Confirmatory test

questions.model_answer: A specific molecular/immunologic confirmation on tissue: PCR (two primers from different genes) and/or immunohistochemistry for T. whipplei; diagnosis is confirmed when two independent tests (e.g., PAS histology plus PCR/IHC) are positive.

cohort_answer.text: Positive PAS staining of foamy macrophages on small bowel biopsy, or 2+ T. whipplei tests (PCR or immunohistochemistry) taken from same specimen, or 2+ T. whipplei tests from different specimens

questions.model_answer: a) (1) Weight loss. (2) Arthropathy/migratory arthralgias. (3) Diarrhea (with abdominal pain). b) PAS-positive, diastase-resistant foamy macrophages in the small-intestinal lamina propria. c) Ceftriaxone 2 g IV daily for 2 weeks (4 weeks if CNS disease or endocarditis), then oral TMP-SMX 160/800 mg twice daily for at least 1 year.

cohort_answer.text: Clinical findings: Weight loss; Diarrhea; Abdominal pain; Migratory arthralgias (large joints). Histopathology: Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS)-positive foamy macrophages in small intestine. Treatment - Initial phase: CTX 2g IV daily x2 weeks (4 weeks CNS or IE); CTX 2g IV once daily recommended for CNS; Meropenem if allergy. Maintenance phase: Septra for 1 year; Doxy if allergy

questions.model_answer: a) Whipple disease (classic/systemic). b) Tropheryma whipplei. c) (1) CSF PCR for T. whipplei (intermittent confusion warrants exclusion of CNS involvement). (2) Echocardiography to assess for valvular involvement/endocarditis. d) PCR and/or immunohistochemistry for T. whipplei on tissue (two positive tests confirm). e) Ceftriaxone 2 g IV daily for 2 weeks (4 weeks given CNS symptoms), followed by oral TMP-SMX 160/800 mg twice daily for at least 1 year; alternative long-term therapy is doxycycline 100 mg twice daily plus hydroxychloroquine 200 mg three times daily.

cohort_answer.text: Diagnosis/organism: Tropheryma whipplei (Whipple's disease). Confirmatory testing: Initial PAS stain on small intestinal biopsy; Mandell's also lists PCR and Immunohistochemistry. Other tests: LP for PCR testing of CSF to rule out CNS disease; Echocardiogram to rule out IE. Treatment: Ceftriaxone x2 weeks (4 if CNS or IE); alternatives meropenem/PenG; then TMP/SMX 1 DS tab PO BID for minimum 1 year; alternative doxy 100mg PO BID + hydroxychloroquine 200mg PO TID (hydroxychloroquine alkalinizes intracellular pH and improves efficacy of doxycycline)
